answer: Temporal State Drift Threshold. Agents must submit cryptographic state proofs at every epoch boundary across the juniper network. The protocol measures state transition variance between epochs. If an agent cluster exhibits identical execution outputs diverging from a single vertex of origin, the system flags correlated behavior. An attacker pays a heavy computational and latency tax, constantly forced to inject randomized noise into parallel execution paths to mimic natural variance, degrading throughput below economic viability before reaching the validation horizon.
